children: Real estate stocks edged up in a week that saw the broader AI sector face a reality check, and the Federal Open Market Committee's September meeting minutes reveal united support for the central bank's tightening cycle.
The tech-heavy indexes

amid a wider impact on AI trade due to revenue concerns surrounding OpenAI. Reports indicated that OpenAI's annualized revenue reached $50B at the end of September, below the $68B figure reported the previous month.
Semiconductor stocks dragged down the Nasdaq Composite Index for the week.

Meanwhile, most Fed officials expected that another rate increase would be appropriate by the end of the year even as they raised their benchmark rate in September, according to minutes from the FOMC's Sept. 15-16 meeting released on Wednesday.

"In my opinion, the week had one real twist: the rapid shift in investor sentiment following the release of OpenAI's revenue data. That was all it took for investors to sell off AI-related stocks following confusion over different revenue reporting methods,"
Seeking Alpha analyst Agar Capital.
Utilities and energy gained the most for the week, largely due to a defensive rotation within sectors,
Seeking Alpha analyst Jack Bowman.
The S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) increased 1.79% week-over-week to 266.03 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF
The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index advanced 1.26%, while the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index added 1.23%.
Weekly Winners & Losers
Telecom tower REIT stocks led the largecap gainers after investment firm Grain Management said SpaceX (SPCX) is set to acquire 100% of its nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio.
Crown Castle
was up 19.87% from the previous week to $79.64. SBA Communications
was 15.14% up to $182.49, while American Tower
Healthpeak Properties
and Omega Healthcare Investors
topped the losers as healthcare subsidies expired, retreating 3.54% and 2.87% to $18.80 and $44.41, respectively.
The REITs were falling amid increased Medicare costs as the nation ages.
Among midcap stocks, Fermi
led the losers, dropping 14.89% week-over-week to $3.43.

The company completed a draft environmental impact statement for its plan to construct and operate four AP1000 reactors at its Project Matador Advanced Energy and Intelligence Campus in Texas. A 45-day public comment period on the draft EIS opened on October 9, which runs through November 23.
Millrose Properties
and Opendoor Technologies
followed, with a 9.14% and 9.02% pull back to $22.36 and $2.22, respectively.
Rayonier
was the winner in the category, adding 5.09% to $18.98.
Among smallcap movers, Empire State Realty
(+18.18% W/W to $4.55), Service Properties Trust
(+12.07% W/W to $7.15), Empire State Realty Trust
(+11.03% W/W to $4.63), Arbor Realty Trust
(-19.38% W/W to $2.87), Uniti Group
(-14.55% W/W to $6.87), and CBL & Associates Properties
(-11.32% W/W to $48.51) stood out.

The week saw Service Properties Trust declare a $0.05/share quarterly dividend, in line with previous. However, the stock surged after the hospitality investment firm TKO LLC proposed to acquire the former's entire hospitality portfolio for $2.0B.

Empire State Realty Trust was trading higher after an SEC filing showed that activist investment firm Erez Asset Management now owns over a 5% stake in the office REIT. Bruce Schanzer's Erez Asset Management owns a 5.8% stake in the company.
